customer_updates.name: SMRUTISIKHA PRADHAN
customer_updates.text:
• Cannon Pav Bhaji is one of Mumbai's most famous street food destinations, located opposite CSMT.
• Established in 1975 by a former Indian Army veteran, it has been serving Mumbaikars and travelers for decades.
• Known for its rich, buttery, and flavorful pav bhaji made in the traditional Mumbai style.
• The pav is perfectly toasted with butter and pairs wonderfully with the delicious bhaji.
• The place has a unique old-Mumbai charm and is an important part of the city's food heritage.
• Despite being a simple standing food stall, it attracts food lovers from across India.
• Quick service, authentic taste, and a nostalgic atmosphere make the experience memorable.
• A must-visit spot for anyone who wants to enjoy Mumbai's legendary pav bhaji and experience a piece of the city's culinary history.

Overall: Great taste, rich history, and a true Mumbai street-food experience. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Pardeshi
featured_reviews.review_text: Canon Pav Bhaji did not live up to the hype at all. I have had much better pav bhaji at many other places. I ordered one Amul Butter Pav Bhaji and one Amul Butter Cheese Pav Bhaji. Both were extremely bland and lacked proper spices. There was an excessive amount of butter added, to the point that only butter’s taste was overpowering everything else—no real flavor of the bhaji could be felt. The pav bhaji was not even served properly hot, which made the experience worse. On top of that, the prices are very high for the quality and taste offered. This review is purely based on my personal experience, and unfortunately, it was very disappointing.

featured_reviews.name: Sachin Sonawane
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Cannon Pav Bhaji near CST and, unfortunately, the experience was quite disappointing. We tried several items Pav Bhaji, Sheera, Sabudana Khichdi and Lassi and to be frank, everything was absolutely tasteless. For a place that is always crowded and located in such a prime spot, I genuinely expected much better in terms of flavour and quality.

The Pav Bhaji lacked the rich, buttery taste and balanced spices that you normally find even at simple street side stalls across Mumbai. The Sheera was bland and lacked the aroma and sweetness that make it enjoyable. Sabudana Khichdi, which is usually comforting and flavourful, felt underwhelming as well. Even the Lassi didn’t have the freshness or thickness you would hope for.

It feels like the only advantage this place has is its central location right outside CST, which naturally attracts tourists and daily commuters. In contrast, some of the other nearby stalls actually serve tastier food at far more economical prices.

Overall, Cannon Pav Bhaji didn’t live up to its hype or its location. If you’re looking for flavourful, satisfying Mumbai street food, you’re better off exploring the smaller stalls around the area.

Its a quite old place with its unchanged taste of food, especially their Pav-bhaji. This outlet was started by a retired military officer. Hence, the name "CANNON". Also, this place employess mostly womens who are widows of miltary personnel's. However, I am not really sure about this fact but yes this place employees womens which is a great example of women empowerment. Whatever the story is the Pav-Bhaji here is one of the best in Mumbai if not the best ! A must try if you are visting Mumbai ! Apart from pav-bhaji the other dishes you can try is gulab jamun, gahar halwa, sabudana khichdi, vada pav, besan ladu etc. They also have chaas, lassi etc as well which goes pretty well with the pav bhaji !!!

featured_reviews.name: Vainateya Sahasrabudhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre in Mumbai my grandfather used to take me to have pav bhaji 2000 to 2014. Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is a renowned destination for street food enthusiasts, serving mouth-watering pav bhaji that has captured the hearts of many. This iconic eatery has earned a reputation for its delicious food, prompt service, and cozy ambiance.

Ambiance
The ambiance at Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is warm and inviting, perfect for a quick bite or a casual meal with friends and family. The decor is minimal, but the vibrant atmosphere and aroma of freshly cooked food make up for it.

Menu and Offerings
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre's menu is centered around its signature dish, pav bhaji, which is a flavorful mix of vegetables cooked in a rich tomato-based gravy, served with soft, buttery pav bread. Some popular items on the menu include-
- *Pav Bhaji*: The star of the show, made with a medley of vegetables and spices, served with pav bread.
- *Special Pav Bhaji*: A variation of the classic dish, made with extra butter and spices.

Quality and Taste
The quality and taste of Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre's offerings are exceptional. The pav bhaji is cooked to perfection, with a rich, buttery flavor that's hard to resist. Customers rave about the delicious food, and many have returned for years, making it a testament to the eatery's consistency.

Service
The service at Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is prompt and efficient, ensuring that customers receive their orders quickly and without any hassle. The staff is friendly and courteous, adding to the overall positive experience.

Value for Money
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre offers excellent value for money, with prices starting from around ₹120-₹200 per person for a meal. Given the quality and quantity of food, it's a steal.

Tips
- Visit Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre during off-peak hours to avoid crowds.
- Try the special pav bhaji for an extra-rich flavor experience.
- Pair your pav bhaji with a buttermilk, lassi or cold drink for a refreshing contrast.

Online Ordering and Delivery
For those who prefer the convenience of home delivery, Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre offers online ordering through platforms like Justdial and Zomato. This allows customers to enjoy their favorite dishes from the comfort of their own homes.

Overall Experience
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is a must-visit destination for anyone looking to experience the best of Mumbai's street food scene. With its delicious pav bhaji, prompt service, and excellent value for money, it's a culinary gem that will leave you wanting more.

Rating: 4.5/5 stars.

featured_reviews.name: Anand Mishra (DocAndy)
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stadium Restaurant has always carried a legacy as a classic Parsi eatery in South Mumbai, and expectations are naturally high when you walk in. Unfortunately, the recent experience was quite disappointing and far from what the name represents.
To begin with, a major portion of the menu was unavailable due to a gas issue. No Chinese items and most veg dishes were not being served. While operational issues can happen, there was no proactive communication or effort from the staff to guide customers properly.
We ordered the basics – Bun Maska, Brun Maska, Special Tea, and a Cheese Sandwich.
Bun Maska & Special Tea: This was the only saving grace. The tea had a nice flavor and the bun was fresh. However, the quantity of maska (butter) has reduced significantly compared to what Stadium was known for.
Brun Maska: Very average. The brun itself was fine, but the maska was almost missing – defeating the whole purpose of ordering it.
Cheese Sandwich: Extremely disappointing. It was literally just a slice of cheese placed between bread with poor presentation. No effort, no taste, no value – completely unacceptable.
Service & Ambience:
The service felt lifeless and unresponsive. There was no warmth, no attentiveness, and overall the environment felt dull and uninviting. For a place with such a legacy, this was shocking.
Overall Impression:
It feels like the restaurant is running purely on its old reputation rather than current quality. If things continue like this, it will only dilute the strong legacy they once built.
A Parsi restaurant like Stadium should reflect discipline, consistency, and warmth, but unfortunately, none of that was evident during this visit.
Final Verdict:
⚠️ Needs serious improvement in food quality, service, and management.
If they wish to survive further, these gaps need immediate attention.

featured_reviews.name: ROHAN REDEKAR
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you want to eat authentic and affordable pav bhaji in a bustling city like Mumbai, Lenin Pav Bhaji is a must-try place. This place is famous for its bhaji made with Amul Maska and for its reasonable prices. Every customer who comes here feels the taste of the real Mumbai streets with the first bite.

The main identity of Lenin Pav Bhaji is their bhaji dipped in Amul butter. Fresh vegetables — potatoes, peas, tomatoes, bell peppers, and a wonderful blend of spices — are used while preparing the bhaji. The generous use of Amul Maska on it gives the bhaji a creamy, aromatic, and satisfying taste. The crispy pav roasted on a tava, melted butter on top, and a lemon wedge served with it — this experience attracts every customer again and again.

The prices here are another big feature.  The plain pav bhaji costs around ₹70–₹90, while the special Amul pav bhaji costs around ₹110–₹120. These prices are really affordable for such quality taste. This makes this place a good choice for students, workers, and families.

The service is fast, the staff is polite, and the place is always kept clean. Even in a crowded place, the taste and quality are maintained, which is the success of Lenin pav bhaji.

Overall, Lenin pav bhaji is the perfect blend of authentic Mumbai street food, the magic of Amul mask, and affordable pleasure. This place scores 10 out of 10 in all three aspects - taste, quality, and price.

featured_reviews.name: Karan Beri
featured_reviews.review_text:
Burger King at Churchgate, Mumbai is a fairly decent outlet, especially considering its prime location near the station and the constant crowd in the area. The place is almost always busy, which itself shows how popular it is among students, office-goers, and people just passing by. Seating inside can feel a bit tight during peak hours, but the overall vibe is lively and energetic.
One of the best parts of this outlet is the outside dining area. It’s actually quite nice to sit outdoors, especially in the evenings. You can enjoy your food while watching the busy Churchgate streets, which adds a Mumbai-style charm to the experience. The outside seating makes the place feel more spacious and relaxed compared to the inside area.
Coming to the food, the burgers were decent in taste but not served very hot, which was slightly disappointing. The flavors were good and consistent with Burger King standards, but the temperature could definitely be improved. Fries and sides were okay, nothing exceptional, but still enjoyable. If you’re very particular about freshly hot food, you might feel a small gap there.
The staff was okay—not overly friendly, but not rude either. Given the rush, they seemed a bit hurried, which is understandable. Orders were handled efficiently, and the place was reasonably clean considering the heavy footfall.
Overall, Burger King Churchgate is a good spot for a quick bite, hanging out with friends, or taking a short break. It’s not perfect, but the location, outdoor seating, and consistent taste make it worth visiting, especially when you’re in the area.

featured_reviews.name: Arin Paul
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Bharat, Churchgate, is one of those old-school vegetarian cafés that quietly survives on routine rather than hype. No frills, no experiments, just straightforward food and a steady crowd of office-goers and regulars.

We had Puri Bhaji, Coffee, and Tikki Chole. The puri bhaji was simple and filling, nothing exceptional but nothing to complain about either. The bhaji was mildly spiced, homely in taste, and the puris were fresh enough. The tikki chole was decent; the tikkis were soft and the chole had a familiar North Indian flavour, though it didn’t stand out in any special way. The coffee was basic café-style, served hot, doing its job without trying to impress.

What works in Cafe Bharat’s favour is its budget-friendly pricing, quick service, and convenient location near Churchgate. It’s not a place you’d go out of your way to visit, but if you’re in the area and want a quick, affordable vegetarian meal, it does the job.

The ambience is functional and old-fashioned; clean, but clearly built for efficiency rather than comfort or aesthetics. Service is prompt and no-nonsense.

Overall, Cafe Bharat is reliable, modest, and predictable. Nothing great, nothing bad. Just a simple veg café that knows its role and sticks to it. Suitable for a quick bite, not for culinary excitement.

Food Street, Mumbai – A Taste of Bombay’s Best

Excellent and tasty food is served here at Food Street, Mumbai, a popular destination for anyone who loves authentic Bombay flavors. This place brings together the city’s most famous street foods under one roof, offering a mix of taste, aroma, and tradition that Mumbai is known for. From the spicy kick of vada pav and the buttery goodness of pav bhaji to the tangy bhel puri and crispy sev puri, every dish reflects the city’s rich food culture.

The chefs here prepare each item with care, using fresh ingredients and maintaining the original Bombay taste that food lovers crave. Whether you prefer light snacks or filling meals, there’s something for everyone. The lively atmosphere, quick service, and friendly staff make dining here an enjoyable experience.

Food Street isn’t just a place to eat—it’s a celebration of Mumbai’s vibrant street food heritage. Locals come here to relive nostalgic flavors, while visitors get a true introduction to the city’s culinary charm. If you’re in Mumbai and looking for delicious, authentic, and affordable food, Food Street is the perfect stop to satisfy your hunger and enjoy Bombay’s famous taste in every bite.

Whether you’re catching up with a friend, working on your laptop, or simply enjoying a slow meal, Earth Café creates an atmosphere that encourages you to linger a little longer.

The food is where the café truly shines. Every dish feels fresh, wholesome, and crafted with care. From vibrant salads and nourishing bowls to indulgent yet guilt-free desserts, the menu caters wonderfully to health-conscious diners without compromising on taste. The beverages—especially their coffees and refreshing coolers—are well-balanced and thoughtfully prepared, making them perfect companions to the food.

What stands out most is the attention to detail: warm service, beautifully plated dishes, and a sense of calm that’s rare in the heart of South Mumbai. Earth Café isn’t just a place to eat; it’s an experience—one that leaves you feeling lighter, happier, and eager to return.

Had a great experience at Samrat Veg Restaurant. Their amras puri is the star: the amras had a rich, smooth consistency and paired perfectly with hot, fluffy puris. They also serve bhaji on the side, which elevates the whole meal and makes it even more satisfying.

We also tried the chole bhature, and it definitely lived up to expectations: flavourful, indulgent, and well-prepared. The ambience is spacious and comfortable, making it a good spot for both quick meals and relaxed dining plans.

Overall, a solid place in South Mumbai if you're craving a wholesome, classic veg meal.

For more honest food reviews, check out @benecia.recommends on IG ✨

featured_reviews.name: Divyanshi Mahajan
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving the best aamras puri in Mumbai, this little gem in Churchgate is my absolute go-to. Just a couple of minutes’ walk from Marine Drive, the location itself is a treat—especially with that beautiful stroll by the sea before or after your meal.

The aamras here is hands down one of the best in the city—fresh, rich, and perfectly sweet. Paired with hot puris, it’s pure comfort on a plate. The rest of the food is equally good, making it a solid spot for a satisfying meal.

Prices are decent, the service is quick, and everything feels clean and well-maintained.

Simple, satisfying, and consistently good—this place never disappoints.

featured_reviews.name: H Nanda
featured_reviews.review_text: Located near churchgate metro station this is a well known vegetarian restaurant frequented by office goers as well as family groups.  Currently this is probably  the only restaurant in the area.  (Shortly the well known Bengaluru based Cafe Rameshwaram is scheduled to open, but it is expected to be a full south Indian) this restaurant is known for its Gujarati dishes and the popular one is the thali.  It's unlimited   with a large number of items, the preparation and taste is good.  The waiters are smartly dressed and present a good service.  Visited this restaurant many times.  Apart from thali have tried their biryani which tastes good.  Nice atmosphere where one can enjoy food.  Weekends and holidays will have wait time.  There is a small waiting area outside.  There are paid parking (roadside) on the CCI ( cricket club of India) and other nearby roads which I suggest to be used as traffic police crane regularly makes rounds in this area.  There is a bakery just outside, which is again popular for pastries chocolates and others bakery items.

featured_reviews.name: Sandeep Mahajan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Over rated restaurant simply as it's in advantageous location and quite old. Famous for its thali but we called a la carte this time.

Chole Bhature.... Bhatures were actually Maida Puris. Size also small.

Daal Dhokli- Little better but Dhokli was totally mashed.

Vegetable Au Gratin was better if the lot.

featured_reviews.name: Kunal Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: Samrat Hotel serves decent, tasty North- and South-Indian, Punjabi food with a modest but clean ambience and friendly staff. The seating is fairly spacious and service is usually prompt, making it a good spot for a quick meal or casual dinner. Crockery or freshness feels just average — but overall it strikes a decent balance of quality, and convenience for the price. Menu is bit expensive but given the location of south Mumbai cant complain about it.

featured_reviews.name: Siddharth Kumar Das
featured_reviews.review_text:
Food was prepared good but the taste was not that great as expected.
The service was a bit slow.
There were enough waiters and staff.
There is a valet parking chargeable at 100₹

The restaurant was clean and hygienic.
The naans were good.
But the price was extremely costly.
A garlic naan is ₹160 and any vegetables start from 450₹.

The tables are very close-by too each other.
And there was a queue always for toilet.
Not expected.
Like if you are charging so much, then you should provide equal service.

featured_reviews.name: Adrian Rodrigues
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best places to come for a Thali Lunch. Not sure about the other items on the menu budgeting by the taste of everything we had on the thali. I'm sure their other menu items would also be equally tasty. This is a pure veg restaurant and they do not serve any non veg or alcohol. There is wale parking available so it's ok if you travel here by your own vehicle. The valley parking is chargeable though. The ambience and seating and staff are really good. If you go during peak hours you may have to wait to get a table so it is always better to go a little early. Very close to the Aqua line Churchgate Metro Station so it is very easily accessible even by foot. The pricing for the thali is extremely reasonable for this part of the city and I guess you will get your best value for money if you order the thali.
They have clean washrooms here too.

featured_reviews.name: Rupesh Tayde
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you're looking for a hearty, vegetarian lunch, Samrat is a great place, It’s a very reliable spot that focuses on clean, traditional flavors rather than anything too fancy.

​I highly recommend their lunch thalis. The spread is generous, featuring a variety of seasonal vegetables, dals, and fresh breads that make for a very satisfying meal. The food is consistently good and feels like a proper, authentic meal.
